Hi Samantha / Amit — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on: 

1) Goal: collect ~250 representative user prompts (mix of happy-path and edge cases) so we can run a focused eval and recommend a production model/config.
2) Priority slices: billing questions, policy-compliance queries, and multi-turn troubleshooting flows (these drove most of the latency/quality tradeoffs).
3) Deliverables we’ll provide: short benchmark report with model recommendations, a redaction checklist, and a one-week prompt evaluation sprint plan.

Immediate next steps (action owners):
- ClearBridge: upload sample prompts to the shared folder or paste into the attached CSV template (prompt_capture_template.csv). We need 50–100 ASAP to unblock initial bench. (Amit / Samantha)
- Redwood (Ben + Connor): run lightweight benchmarks across three representative variants and share latency/cost/accuracy tradeoffs.
- Redwood CS (Marissa): produce redaction checklist and instructions for safe sampling.

What we need from you in this first batch: 
- 50–100 de-identified prompts covering the three priority slices above. If you must include real PII for fidelity, mark the row and we will redact manually but prefer already-sanitized examples.
- Notes for any prompts that are known to be frequent failure modes today (e.g., hallucinations about account balances, legal/regulatory phrasing).

I’ve attached a prompt_capture_template.csv and our redaction guidelines draft. Also linking a short example benchmark we ran internally to show the format of the deliverable.

Timeline: if we get the first 50 by EOD Friday PST (5/18), we can return a short bench and recommended model slice by Wednesday 5/23. Does that work on your end?

Best,
Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Samantha — quick answers and what we’ll run for the first pass: 

1) Region: we can run the evaluation in EU or US. For the initial lightweight bench (first 50 prompts) we typically run in the closest region to your users; indicate a preference in the CSV header and we’ll honor it.

2) Redaction quick-ref: see excerpt below (we'll attach a one-page quick-reference in the next message):
- Replace emails with [EMAIL], phone numbers with [PHONE], names with [PERSON_NAME]. Keep dates/timestamps where they matter for the conversational context.
- If the prompt references account-specific IDs that matter to routing logic, replace the numeric token but keep the pattern (e.g., ACC-XXXX -> ACC-1234).

3) Recommended models / recommended starting configs (first-pass):
- "compact" (low-latency): 7B-class + q4_0 quantization — target for user-facing autocomplete and quick lookups.
- "balanced" (tradeoff): 13B-class optimized with 8k context — good for multi-turn troubleshooting and factual recall.
- "high-fidelity" (safety/accuracy): 33B+ class with selective KV caching and higher temperature control — use for complex policy/legal responses.

Bench approach we will run (what you’ll see in the deliverable):
- Latency (p50/p95), cost per 1k tokens, and exact-match / semantic-similarity on a small verified gold-set we create from your samples.
- Regression checks: we will run the new models against a short suite of known-edge-case prompts you mark as "regression_critical" so we can alert if hallucination rates increase vs. your baseline.

Attachments included in this email: prompt_capture_template.csv (CSV), redaction_guidelines_v1.pdf (full guidelines). I’ve also dropped a short benchmark stub that shows the format we'll share.

If it helps, Ben and I can host a 30-minute intake session with your product analyst to walk the template while they paste prompts. Ben — can you take the intake call if they want it?

Thanks,
Connor
